hypothesis.title: Recommendation OOM loop from unbounded cache growing to 1.9GiB
hypothesis.summary: The recommendation service has an unbounded in-memory cache that grows to 1.9GiB, causing heap exhaustion and full-GC pressure. Every ~10-15 minutes the pod is OOMKilled and restarts, dropping in-flight requests. Frontend sees periodic bursts of MemoryError responses from recommendation, triggering the 5xx alert. This matches the known pattern from PM-2026-05-04.
hypothesis.reasoning: The alert fired on frontend's 5xx error rate. Tracing the errors upstream: 83% of failing frontend traces end in recommendation (evidence traces:frontend:summary), and 94% of failing recommendation traces fail within recommendation itself (traces:recommendation:summary). The deepest error in multiple traces is "MemoryError: cache grew to 1.9GiB" originating from recommendation. The recommendation pod was OOMKilled 4 times (k8s:recommendation:pod_status), and memory utilization peaked at 95% of limit (metrics:recommendation:memory_utilization). Logs show "heap usage above 90% after full GC" 384 times starting 30 minutes before the alert (logs:recommendation:1), indicating memory pressure and GC thrashing before the OOM kills. The error pattern matches postmortem PM-2026-05-04 exactly: an unbounded product cache in recommendation causing a sawtooth OOM loop. The ad service deploy (changes:ad:deploy:0) happened 38 minutes before the alert but ad is not on the failing call path (frontend → recommendation), so it's a red herring. Product-catalog is healthy (0.4% error rate, 18ms p95). The currency restart (k8s:currency:pod_status) is also unrelated—currency is not in the failing traces. This is a memory leak in recommendation causing periodic OOMKills and error bursts.

supporting_evidence.why_it_matters: Pod was OOMKilled 4 times, confirming memory exhaustion is causing restarts and service disruption.
Failing trace shows the error originates in recommendation with 'MemoryError: cache grew to 1.9GiB', proving the root cause.
384 warnings of heap above 90% after full GC starting 30m before alert indicate memory leak and GC thrashing before OOM.
Memory peaked at 95% of limit with a sawtooth pattern consistent with leak-then-OOM-then-restart cycle.
94% of failing recommendation traces fail within recommendation itself, ruling out downstream dependencies.
2,448 frontend errors calling recommendation with the same MemoryError confirm the propagation path to the alerting service.

suggested_actions.title: Restart recommendation deployment to temporarily clear the cache and restore service
suggested_actions.rationale: Clears the unbounded cache and stops the OOM loop immediately. This is the safest first step to restore service while investigating the code fix.

suggested_actions.title: Increase memory limit for recommendation to buy time for a code fix
suggested_actions.rationale: Extends the time between OOM kills, reducing error bursts. However, this only delays the problem if the cache truly has no eviction policy.

suggested_actions.title: Review and deploy a fix for the unbounded product cache in recommendation
suggested_actions.rationale: The root cause is a code defect (unbounded cache). Add an LRU eviction policy or size limit to the cache, referencing PM-2026-05-04 for the previous fix.

alternatives.why_less_likely: Product-catalog metrics are healthy (0.4% error rate, 18ms p95, stable CPU/memory). Only 1 of 200 traces failed, and 94% of recommendation errors originate in recommendation itself, not downstream.
